# `ccl` standard library

The `ccl` module implements the [Categorical Configuration Language (CCL)](https://github.com/chshersh/ccl)
parser, data model, deterministic serializer, and `#!` compile-time structural encoder/decoder.

```{.dva .run}
#use ccl
```

## Data model

The core document model represents nested, indentation-delimited key-value entries:

```{.dva .run}
#type Strings String{}

#type CclVal <
   Str(String),
   Block(CclDoc)
>

#type CclEntry (
   key: String,
   val: CclVal,
   line: Int,
   col: Int
)

#type CclEntries CclEntry{}

#type CclDoc CclEntry{}
```

## Structural encoding and decoding (`#!`)

`ccl` provides compile-time structural codecs for records, tuples, enums, options, arrays, maps, primitives, and `CclDoc`:

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ccl::encode` | `val => String` | Serialize any record, map, or `CclDoc` into a canonical CCL string |
| `ccl::decode` | `#! T, String => < T | Error >` | Parse CCL text and decode into target type `T` |
| `ccl::decode_file` | `#! T, String => < T | Error >` | Read a file from disk and decode its CCL contents into `T` |
| `ccl::to_doc` | `val => CclDoc` | Convert any record, map, or `CclDoc` into a `CclDoc` |
| `ccl::to_ccl_val` | `val => CclVal` | Convert any value into a `CclVal` |
| `ccl::decode_doc` | `#! T, CclDoc => < T | Error >` | Decode a parsed `CclDoc` into target type `T` |
| `ccl::decode_val` | `#! T, CclVal => < T | Error >` | Decode a `CclVal` into target type `T` |

### Codec conventions

- **Forward-compatible records (`[(..)]`)**: Unknown keys in input are ignored. Missing keys use declared field defaults (`f.default`), `<-->` for option fields (`<P|>`), or `f.type.zero` for emptyable containers (`E{}`, `K ^ V`); an `Error` is returned only when a required non-option field with no default is missing.
- **External enum tagging (`[<..>]`)**: Unit variants encode and decode as plain strings (`"VariantName"`), while payload variants encode and decode as single-entry blocks (`VariantName = payload`).
- **Boolean flags (`[<>]`)**: `ccl::to_ccl_val` / `ccl::encode` serializes `<+>` as `"true"` and `<->` as `"false"`. In `ccl::decode_val`, a string entry (`Str s`) decodes to `<+>` (true) when `s` is `"true"`, `"1"`, or `"yes"`, and decodes to `<->` (false) when `s` is `"false"`, `"0"`, or `"no"`; any other string or a block entry returns an `Error`.

```{.dva .partial}
#type ServerCfg (
   host: String = "127.0.0.1",
   port: Int = 8080,
   tls: <> = <->,
   cert_path: < String | >,
   tags: String{}
)

text = ccl::encode(ServerCfg("0.0.0.0", 9090, <+>, <+ "/etc/ssl/cert.pem" +>, String{}("api", "prod")))
cfg = ccl::decode(ServerCfg, text)!!
```

## Document parsing and query helpers

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ccl::parse` | `String, String => < CclDoc | Error >` | Parse CCL text with an associated source path for diagnostics |
| `ccl::parse_file` | `String => < CclDoc | Error >` | Read and parse a CCL configuration file from disk |
| `ccl::to_ccl` | `CclDoc => String` | Serialize a `CclDoc` into a canonical, deterministic CCL string |
| `ccl::has` | `CclDoc, String => <>` | Check if a top-level key exists in the document |
| `ccl::get` | `CclDoc, String => < String | >` | Retrieve the string value of a top-level key |
| `ccl::get_section` | `CclDoc, String => < CclDoc | >` | Retrieve a nested block section as a sub-document |
| `ccl::get_list` | `CclDoc, String => < Strings | >` | Retrieve `= item` list entries inside the named section |
| `ccl::entries_for` | `CclDoc, String => Strings` | Retrieve all string values for repeated occurrences of a key |

```{.dva .partial}
doc = ccl::parse("name = demo\nversion = 0.1.0", "edva.ccl")!!
name = ccl::get(doc, "name") | n => n | "unknown"
```
